mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within a month signals weakening labor market conditions, which leads to reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) signals a weakening demand environment, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 60-day forward returns in contraction periods are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% within a month signals strengthening supply-side conditions, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4% and payroll employment (PAYEMS) increases by more than 200,000 in a month, it signals a tight labor market with wage pressures, which can lead to inflation and monetary tightening, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% and PAYEMS increases > 200,000 in 1 month
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) decline by more than 10% year-over-year and consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 2% year-over-year, it signals a demand-side slowdown coupled with inflationary pressures, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST declines > 10% YoY and CPIAUCSL increases > 2% YoY
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 3% signals inflationary pressures, which typically leads to monetary tightening and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: When real GDP (GDPC1) growth is negative for two consecutive quarters, it signals a recessionary environment, which leads to reduced corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 negative growth for 2 consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal.
